title: Xanthe and the Contact
premise: Petra Amberdale, a whistle-blower living under four names, receives a debt notice from a stranger claiming she owes him for a favor that saved her life years ago—a favor she never knew happened. The stranger, a fixer named Corvin, demands payment in the form of the sealed testimony that could expose a private military consortium's massacre, the very secret Petra has guarded through four identities. As Petra investigates whether Corvin is her savior or her executioner, she discovers he is both: the man who pulled her from the fire and the man hired to retrieve what she carries. In the end, Petra chooses to burn the testimony publicly rather than trade it privately, sacrificing her invisibility forever but forcing the justice she once fled—and paying for it with the only name she has left.
about_author: Ansel Thornbury is the pen name of a former compliance investigator who spent a decade inside institutions that preferred silence. He writes thrillers about people who know exactly how systems fail because they've watched them do it.

chapters.title: The Fourth Name
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. Living as 'Mara Voss' in a Rotterdam boarding house, Petra takes an anonymous leak case for cash, establishing her tradecraft and paranoia. A routine dead-drop goes wrong when she finds a note addressed not to Mara Voss but to 'Petra'—a name no one alive should know. Emotional beat: the cold shock of being seen.

chapters.title: Interest Owed
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. She runs, burns the Rotterdam identity, and surfaces in Marseille as 'Claire.' But Corvin finds her within hours—no threats, just a ledger showing a debt: a rescue from a fire in Vilnius nine years ago that she never knew occurred. He gives her seven days to pay. Emotional beat: vertigo; her entire history rewritten.

chapters.title: What the Fire Hid
chapters.summary: Petra's POV, with a flashback chapter. Reconstructing Vilnius, Petra realizes someone extracted her from the consortium's purge before it consumed her—but the records show the rescuer died there. If Corvin is lying about being her savior, why does he know details only the dead man could? Emotional beat: grief resurfacing through suspicion.

chapters.title: The Consortium's Quiet Men
chapters.summary: Corvin's POV. We see his side: hired by the consortium's lawyer to retrieve the testimony, but bound by an older contract—the dead rescuer was his brother, and the favor was real. Corvin intends to collect the debt honestly, even if his employers want Petra erased after delivery. Emotional beat: a man torn between two obligations.

chapters.title: Seven Days, Four Names
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. Racing across safehouses, Petra tests Corvin: feeding each identity a different version of the testimony's location to find who's leaking to the consortium. One name comes back compromised—someone inside her old network is still reporting on her. Emotional beat: the loneliness of trust as a tactical decision.

chapters.title: The Broker in the Chapel
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. She meets the consortium's intermediary, Veyra, in a deconsecrated chapel, pretending to negotiate. Veyra offers more than money: full restoration of one true identity, amnesty, a life. All Petra must do is hand over the testimony quietly—before Corvin can deliver it. Emotional beat: temptation dressed as mercy.

chapters.title: Brother's Ledger
chapters.summary: Corvin's POV. Corvin discovers the consortium never intended to honor any deal—they've scheduled Petra's death for the day after delivery, and his own too. Confronting the memory of his brother, who died believing debts should be paid in truth, Corvin decides which contract matters. Emotional beat: conversion under pressure.

chapters.title: Dead Drop at Dawn
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. Petra and Corvin, now uneasy allies, set a trap: a fake delivery to draw out Veyra's kill team while the real testimony moves. The trap half-works—Veyra takes the bait but escapes, and Petra learns the consortium has a fallback: her sister, located after nine years of silence. Emotional beat: fear turning personal.

chapters.title: The Price of the Secret
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. Cornered at a coastal safehouse with her sister as leverage, Petra faces the choice the whole book has built toward: trade the testimony for safety, or destroy her invisibility by making it public. With Corvin holding off the team, she uploads everything—every name, every file—to every outlet at once. Emotional beat: terror transfigured into resolve.

chapters.title: One Name Left
chapters.summary: Petra's POV, coda. The consortium collapses into indictments; Veyra is arrested; the sister is safe but estranged by the danger. Petra, stripped of all four names by exposure, sits with Corvin over the settled ledger and chooses a fifth name—her own, finally spoken aloud. Emotional beat: quiet, costly peace.
